notShipped.why: design and planning records for this repository. They explain why a rule exists; they are not needed to follow it.
the published documentation site's own sources. A user reads the built site; the archive does not carry a second copy of it.
generated documentation output, rebuilt from docs-site by the pages workflow.
the blog's own sources, published by a separate workflow.
Remotion project for promotional renders. Its output is a rendered file, not something the installer ships.
upstream stageshow scenes, deliberately not vendored (see check-motion-kit.mjs). A contract naming them names the upstream repository, not this archive.

the desktop shell (apps/shell: Next.js UI + Tauri shell). It is published as its own signed-unsigned desktop artifact, not inside the CLI tarball: the archive excludes node_modules, so a shipped copy could not be run by the installer anyway. DESIGN.md names apps/shell/ui because the visual contract must cover its sources, which live in the repository.

upstream.why: a directory inside the upstream stageshow repository. The contract names it to say what is deliberately not here; it is not a path this archive could ever contain.
upstream file whose NOTICE.md places it outside the MIT grant. Named so the prohibition is concrete.
